issues.body:
consumeResultStream(streamPromise) awaits store.queryBindings(query) and then runs `for await (const _row of stream) rows++`. store.queryBindings resolves to `asResultStream(new ResultStream(() => this.queryBindingsStream(sparql)))` (js/src/store.ts:339). ResultStream (js/src/result-stream.ts) is a deliberately browser-safe EventEmitter-subset class: it implements on/addListener/once/removeListener/off/emit/read/pause/resume/destroy, but it defines NEITHER [Symbol.asyncIterator] NOR [Symbol.iterator] (a grep over js/src shows the only Symbol.iterator implementations live in bindings.ts and dataset.ts; every existing consumer in js/test/stream.test.mjs uses on('data')/read()/pause()). `for await...of` looks up Symbol.asyncIterator, falls back to Symbol.iterator, finds neither, and throws. I confirmed this empirically against a structural stand-in with the same member set: `TypeError: s is not async iterable`.

The throw fires in measureAsync's warm-up `await fn()` for the FIRST query in the Object.entries(QUERIES) loop, so it rejects out of the module's top-level await: the advisory JSON block is never printed, store.free() is never reached, and `npm run bench` exits non-zero. The adjacent line `measure(() => [...store.queryBindingsStream(query)].length)` works only because queryBindingsStream is a Generator (which does have Symbol.iterator) — that contrast is why the bug is easy to miss.

Impact is confined to the manual advisory bench (js/package.json `bench` script; not run in CI, and the repo's own research notes record this script as unregistered/non-canonical). The published @jeswr/sparq package and the fromBytes feature are unaffected. But the code added by this PR is non-functional as written, so it cannot be approved as correct and complete. This is the same finding as round 3, at the same severity, on unchanged code.
issues.title: consumeResultStream() does `for await` over the non-async-iterable RDF/JS ResultStream — throws TypeError and aborts the sparq bench block (carried unfixed from round 3)

issues.body: fromBytes calls WasmStore.loadBytes / loadBytesWithBase, which only exist when sparq-wasm is built with the bytes-ingest feature. build:wasm now enables it (js/package.json), but build:wasm:lean does not, so on a lean bundle the call fails with 'WasmStore.loadBytes is not a function' rather than a clear 'byte ingest not available in this build' message. This is a documented, intentional tradeoff (the doc-comment notes dataset/compressed modes have no byte variants, and crates/sparq-wasm/src/bytes.rs states the lean default bundle deliberately carries zero byte-ingest code so wasm_bundle_bytes stays byte-identical), and it does not affect the published package. Non-blocking; carried unaddressed from rounds 1-3.
issues.fix_hint: Optionally guard for a clearer failure on lean builds: `if (typeof WasmStore.loadBytes !== 'function') throw new Error('fromBytes requires a wasm bundle built with the bytes-ingest feature; use fromString on the lean bundle');` after `await init()`. Not required for correctness of the published package.
issues.title: fromBytes fails with an opaque TypeError on the lean wasm bundle, which omits bytes-ingest

verdict.summary: Round 4 is materially identical to round 3: the published-package change is still correct, and the round-3 major bench defect is still unfixed — js/bench/vs-oxigraph.mjs at HEAD is byte-for-byte the code round 3 flagged. PUBLISHED PACKAGE (unchanged, correct and complete): SparqStore.fromBytes delegates to the opt-in feature-gated bindings in crates/sparq-wasm/src/bytes.rs, which fail-closed-validate UTF-8 (std::str::from_utf8 -> JsError; never a panic or lossy decode) then reuse the EXISTING Graph::load_str / load_str_with_base path, so the store is byte-identical to string ingest. Zero new deps; bytes-ingest is OFF by default so the lean bundle is untouched; build:wasm enables it; .d.ts and SKILL.md are synced. The added JS test is non-vacuous: DATA parses to 6 triples, so a silently-empty fromBytes store fails the size assertion, and the queryJson comparison is a real result-equivalence check. BENCH DEFECT (carried, unaddressed): consumeResultStream() drains store.queryBindings(query) with `for await...of`. queryBindings returns asResultStream(new ResultStream(...)) (js/src/store.ts:339), and ResultStream (js/src/result-stream.ts) is a browser-safe EventEmitter-subset class exposing on/once/read/pause/resume/destroy but implementing NEITHER Symbol.asyncIterator NOR Symbol.iterator (the only Symbol.iterator impls in js/src are in bindings.ts and dataset.ts). I confirmed the failure empirically against a structural stand-in: `TypeError: s is not async iterable`. It throws in measureAsync's warm-up on the FIRST query, so the sparq block aborts before the advisory JSON prints and before store.free(). The adjacent queryBindingsStream path works only because a Generator has Symbol.iterator. Blast radius is the manual, non-CI advisory bench only, but the newly added code does not run. The round-3 nit (opaque TypeError from fromBytes on the lean bundle) also remains. No injected instructions found in the diff or prior findings.
